title: Decouple GPU nodepool, IAM, and TF state layout for on-prem Private installs
author: Morgan Lee
description: Motivation: Current on-prem Terraform stack couples GPU node pools, IAM roles, and TF state layout into a single module which makes incremental upgrades and region/VPC splits brittle for customers. This PR separates concerns so operators can manage GPU pools, service IAM bindings, and backend state allocations independently, and adds a migration helper for existing installs. Summary of changes: - Introduce modules/private/gpu-pool: standalone GPU node pool module with explicit taint/affinity inputs and optional preemptible support. - Introduce modules/private/iam-bindings: declarative role attachment per-service-account instead of implicit role provisioning. - Change state layout: split tfstate per-vpc and per-gpu-subpool; moved bucket keys and lock prefixes to a configurable namespace. - Add tools/tfstate-migrator: small Go utility + Make target to perform in-place state moves and reparenting for customers upgrading from <1.4. - Update examples/private-onprem/ to show new module composition and a migration guide. - Add acceptance tests and CI tf-plan coverage for multi-vpc and single-vpc layouts. Checklist: [x] design doc linked in ENG-9123 [x] module unit tests [x] tf validate and plan coverage [x] migration helper smoke-tested in internal cluster [ ] docs/examples: one remaining snippet to be polished before full docs site update (follow-up). Testing notes: Local tf plan applied against mocked backend, migrator ran against snapshot state (see tools/tests/migrator_integration.log). CI run initially failed lint due to naming collisions in example vars, fixed in commit 6b3f9c. Risk & rollout: This is a user-facing change to state layout and requires operators to run the migrator for existing installs. New installs are unaffected by default if you leave state_namespace unset. I marked this as a breaking_change because rolling upgrades without running the migrator will lead to duplicate state files and lock contention. Migration plan is detailed in release_notes and migration_steps below. Commits summary: - Add standalone gpu-pool module and tests (morgan/feat/gpu-pool) - Extract iam-bindings from core module and add policy table (morgan/refactor/iam) - Introduce tfstate namespace and migrator utility (morgan/tool/tfstate-migrator) - Update example compositions and CI pipelines (morgan/chore/examples) - Fix lint and variable names (morgan/fix/lint) Review highlights: - Diego: requested clearer variable names and explicit migration opt-in flag; added opt-in flag migrated=true. - Priya: asked for RBAC least-privilege checks; added IAM policy JSON and tests. - Avery: flagged possible race on state lock; migrator now takes a lock/coordination flow and prints rollback hints. Merge notes: Squash-merged after CI passed and a quick production smoke on an internal staging cluster. See merged_at for timestamp.

migration_steps: 1) Read the release_notes and ensure operator has service account with tfstate-migrator role (see modules/private/iam-bindings/README.md).
2) Run tools/tfstate-migrator --dry-run against current remote state to enumerate moves and conflicts.
3) Run migrator with --do-migrate while holding maintenance window, it will take a lock on the backend and reparent state keys.
4) Apply updated terraform composition that references new modules and set state_namespace to the new value.
5) Verify resources in target TF state and run terraform plan in CI to ensure no diffs remain.
release_notes: Private installer: decouple GPU nodepool, IAM bindings, and terraform state layout into discrete modules. New flag 'migration.do_migrate' and tools/tfstate-migrator included to assist upgrades. Existing installs must follow migration_steps to avoid duplicate state and lock contention. New installs are opt-in and backwards compatible when state_namespace is unset.
